To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can control the morphologies, molecular ordering, and alignment of conjugated polymes in thin films by solution processing, and the resulting morphologies have direct impact on charge transport properties of polymer thin films.

the morphology of conjugated polymer active layers is a key factor that significantly affects charge transport characteristics of devices, and that the solution processing strategies can be used to control morphology of polymer thin films for achieving high performance devices.

solution treatment and deposition conditions can be used to control morphology and charge transport of conjugated polymics, and that these effects are related to the molecular ordering and alignment of polymer chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
controlling the molecular ordering, alignment, and charge transport in conjugated polymer thin film.
controlling the molecular ordering, alignment, and charge transport in solution-processed conjugated polymer thin film.
the development of novel processing strategies to control molecular ordering and alignment of conjugated polymer active layer for high performance flexible electronic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
morphology control is one of the key factors that determine charge transport and thus device performance.
solution-processed conjugated polymer thin film morphology is a critical parameter in determining charge transport characteristics and device performance.

the processing strategies discussed in this review have been shown to be effective in controlling the morphology of conjugated polymer films and thus impact charge carrier transport and device performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
morphology control of conjugged polymer thin films is an important and effective approach to enhance charge transport and thus improve device performance.
morphology control of conjugged polymer thin-filims using solution-based processing strategies is a promising way to improve the performance of flexible electronic devices.

the solution processing strategies can be applied to a broad range of conjugated polymeric materials and can be used as an effective tool for morphology control of polymer thin films, thus leading to improved device performances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
morphology of conjugated polymer films is highly dependent on the processing conditions and thus can be controlled by tuning these conditions.
the morphology control of conjugate polymers can significantly impact the device performance.
solution treatment and deposition techniques can be used to tune the molecular ordering and alignment in conjugated polymer thin film, which in turn significantly affects charge transport properties.
